children: The European Union said Friday it
the proposed all-stock merger of Axalta Coating Systems
after the companies agreed to sell assets in ‌Europe to address competition concerns.
The European Commission - the European Union's competition authority - said on Friday that the groups would divest Akzo Nobel's
vehicle refinish coatings business in Europe to a suitable buyer to address ​concerns over the merged company's strong market power that ​could lead to price hikes for repair garages and consumers.

The merger will create a global coatings company with ~$17B in revenue and a broad portfolio across Powder Coatings, Aerospace Coatings, Refinish, Mobility, Marine and Protective Coatings, Industrial Coatings, and Decorative Coatings.
"Receiving the European Commission's approval is an important milestone as we move closer to completing our merger with Axalta," said Greg Poux-Guillaume, AkzoNobel
CEO, who will become CEO of the combined company.
